stories.headline: Chefs Cook Onstage While Violins Cry at The Triple Door
stories.body: Tonight only (July 6), art forms gloriously collide at The Triple Door as celebrated local chefs — including Mutsuko Soma and Kenji Lopez-Alt — lead onstage culinary demos backed by live chamber music. This year's format upgrades to a family-style four-course dinner so ticket holders can watch, listen, and taste all at once. It's the most delicious concert you'll ever attend — or the most melodic dinner.

stories.headline: World-Class Chamber Music Celebrates America's 250th Birthday
stories.body: The Seattle Chamber Music Society's 2026 Summer Festival is built around the composers who shaped the American classical voice — every program features a work meaningfully connected to the U.S., composed here or by an American. Upcoming Seattle-area concerts run July 7, 9, and 12 at Nordstrom Recital Hall, with later stops at Town Hall Seattle, Vashon Center for the Arts, and Bainbridge Performing Arts through July 26. Single tickets are on sale now.

stories.headline: Sea Creatures Await: Aquarium Naturalists Hit Six Seattle Beaches
stories.body: On days with particularly low tides this summer, Seattle Aquarium naturalists lace up their boots and head to six area shorelines — from the Olympic Sculpture Garden Pocket Beach to Golden Gardens — to help visitors identify tide pool finds and share fun marine facts. No ticket required; just show up at low tide and look for the expert in rubber boots. It's free, salty, and probably the best thing you can do on a sunny PNW morning.
stories.location: Multiple beaches citywide · Ongoing low-tide days through summer

stories.headline: The Circus Is Literally for the Birds at Green Lake's Historic Theater
stories.body: Seattle Public Theater's returning cabaret sensation stars poultry and feathered friends in burlesque and acrobatic feats — yes, really — running July 9 through July 25. Evening shows lean into the adult absurdity, while a family-friendly 2pm matinee swaps out the risqué bits for extra circus magic and silliness. Tickets range from $10–$100 at the gorgeous Green Lake venue.

stories.headline: Ballard's Seafoodfest Gets a Rebrand — and a Very Stacked Stage
stories.body: Originally a celebration of Ballard's fishing industry since 1974, Seafoodfest has rebranded this year as Ballard Music & Seafoodfest to spotlight its increasingly stacked musical lineup alongside plates of alder-smoked salmon barbecue, beer-battered shrimp, and buckets of clams. Friday night brings '80s tribute band Nite Wave; Saturday serves up Built to Spill and dream pop-rockers Coral Grief; Sunday closes with a lutefisk-eating contest and a Fleetwood Mac tribute. Free and fun all weekend.

stories.headline: Seattle Center Becomes the World Cup's Living Room All Month
stories.body: Can't score a match ticket? Seattle Center's Let's Play SEA '26 fan hub is the next best thing — a massive free public celebration with indoor and outdoor match screenings, community gatherings, food vendors, and watch parties spread across the Armory, Mural Amphitheatre, and the KEXP viewing spaces throughout the entire tournament. Bring a blanket, embrace the strangers around you, and scream at a very large screen.
stories.location: Seattle Center, Lower Queen Anne · Ongoing through end of World Cup
